items.title: A Rs 5,000 spending cap. A fleet of Defenders, Thars. Welcome to the DUSU election
items.summary: Walking out of Gate Number 4 of the Vishwavidyalaya metro station, students are met with a familiar sight during Delhi University’s election season: pamphlets and posters carrying the names and ballot numbers of ABVP, NSUI and other candidates. But DU’s election guidelines prohibit candidates from using printed campaign material. Newslaundry found that some of the posters being used for canvassing appear handwritten but are actually printed on low-quality paper. Printing shops told us that thousands of such copies can be produced for a relatively low cost. The campaign spectacle extends beyond pamphlets. Early this week, North Campus saw rows of Defenders, Scorpios and Thars being used in rallies, while students also described food, gifts, trips and other outreach activities organised by student groups. The scale of these campaigns raises questions about how the rules governing DU student elections are being followed. items.title: Clash at DU's Law Centre-1 during DUSU campaigning leaves students injured
items.summary: Clashes broke out at Delhi University's Law Centre-1 on Wednesday - the final day of campaigning for the Delhi University Students' Union (DUSU) elections - leaving students injured. According to the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP), the clash broke out outside Law Centre-1 after an argument over the removal of campaign banners. The organisation said three of its members were injured, two with head wounds and one with a fractured hand. DCP (North) Niharika Bhatt of Delhi Police described it as a minor verbal altercation and scuffle between two groups of students that broke out around 5 PM/ According to sources, the disruption also extended to Umang Bhawan and the Campus Law Centre. Heavy police barricading was reported through the area, stretching from Kirori Mal College towards Chhatra Marg. Sources also said that the old Faculty of Law premises were cleared as a precaution. Reportedly, ABVP has also alleged that one of its members suffered a "life-threatening attack" outside Law Centre-1. items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Thursday pulled up the Central government, Delhi University (DU), and the Delhi Police for their failure to control the violence and hooliganism during the campaigning for the Delhi University Students' Union (DUSU) elections. A Division Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia warned that it will stop the counting of the votes if the authorities fail to explain by tomorrow the steps taken by them against candidates and persons violating the law. The polling is scheduled for tomorrow (September 18). "No excuses will be accepted by the Court and we are making it very clear that, though we are not staying or postponing the election but, if we are not satisfied with your action, we can pass a harsher order staying the counting or declaration of results. We feel that unless such orders are passed, no one is going to listen. It’s very, very sad. Please tell us if you are unable to control the situation, we know how to get it done," the Court remarked. items.title: Tryst with the Constitution: The many constitutional questions in the CJP protest order
items.summary: Earlier this month, the Supreme Court issued an order quashing all FIRs registered across India in connection with the student protest led by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP). It permitted the Central government and the Delhi Police to register fresh FIRs with respect to 2,873 individuals having serious criminal antecedents. While the order largely brought to a close criminal proceedings arising out of the protests, its reasoning raises several constitutional questions. Inadequate reasons for quashing the FIRs The Court’s order was passed in applications moved by the Delhi Police and other State governments, which sought the quashing of FIRs registered between July 20-25, during the student protests. Under ordinary circumstances and procedure, a party seeking the quashing of an FIR would be required to approach the respective High Court . However, in this case, the State approached the Supreme Court directly and sought invocation of its powers under Article 142 of the Constitution . The provision enables the Court to pass any order necessary “for doing complete justice” in a matter pending before it. items.title: Fear of court intervention must not stop arbitrators from taking a firm stand: Ciccu Mukhopadhaya
items.summary: Arbitrators should not become hesitant in controlling proceedings merely because they fear that a court may later set aside their award, Senior Advocate Ciccu Mukhopadhaya said on Thursday. Mukhopadhaya said arbitral institutions can help curb delay tactics, but the ultimate responsibility rests with the tribunal. “ It is entirely the job of the Tribunal to control. The Tribunal must have the confidence in itself and not really bother that if the court tomorrow is going to set it aside, so be it. But if you give a well-reasoned order as to why you think the Party should be denied that opportunity again and again, then the court is unlikely that the court will ultimately interfere with it .” The panel was moderated by Shantanu Agarwal, Managing Partner, Lexster Law . It also included Senior Advocate Mahesh Jethmalani , Mahmood Hussain, Founding Partner, M&Co Legal, Dubai , and Olga Tsvetkova, Managing Partner, Brevia Legal, Abu Dhabi, UAE . Mukhopadhyay said parties could delay arbitration at virtually every stage, from appointment of arbitrators and filing of pleadings to document production and adjournment requests. items.title: Kerala court sentences ex-DGP Tomin Thachankary to 4 years jail in disproportionate assets case
items.summary: A vigilance court in Kerala on Thursday sentenced former Kerala Director General of Police (DGP) Tomin J Thachankary to four years rigorous imprisonment for amassing assets disproportionate to his wealth [ State of Kerala v.Tomin J Thachankary ]. Kottayam Enquiry Commissioner and Special Judge (Vigilance) KV Rajaneesh passed the verdict after finding that there was a disproportionate income of over ₹30 lakh, which comes up to over 50% of his known income at the time. " The convict was a senior officer of the Indian Police Service and had held several responsible positions during his service career, including 145 the rank of Director General of Police, Kerala. The higher the public office held, greater is the obligation to maintain the highest standards of integrity and probity. The disproportion of ₹30,84,892.39, constituting 52.33% of the known income, is neither marginal nor insignificant. It represents the unexplained enrichment accumulated during the check period from 2003 to 2007, when the said amount had substantial value, " the Court's judgment stated. items.title: Equal pay for equal work cannot be applied mechanically; experience must be considered: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court recently held that identical job functions and duties alone do not entitle employees to claim "equal pay for equal work" under Article 14 of the Constitution [ GP Sangeetha v. State of Kerala & Ors. ]. A Bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu upheld a higher pay scale for teachers appointed via promotion or transfer due to their prior service experience. Legal standard for pay parity has changed over the years, the Bench remarked. "In the last century, this Court treated equal pay for equal work as an expansive anti-exploitation principle under Articles 14 and 39(d), where the mere sameness of designation was sufficient to claim parity. In this century, however, the doctrine has been recast as a strict test based on service rules. Decisions are legion that equal pay cannot be claimed by merely showing identical work; the claimant-employee must establish complete parity in the source of recruitment, educational qualifications and experience," the Court said. items.title: Litigant cannot be shown the door for NCLAT portal failure: Supreme Court restores appeal filed one day late
items.summary: The Supreme Court recently held that a litigant cannot be denied relief merely on account of a delay in filing an appeal when the delay is caused entirely by a fault on a tribunal or court's e-filing portal [ Regional Provident Fund Commissioner-II v. Ms Mamta Binani and Others ]. A Bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu made the observation in a case where an appeal in an insolvency resolution case was filed with a delay of one day because earlier attempts to e-file the appeal failed due to glitches on the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal's (NCLAT) online portal. “ Should a litigant be shown the door at the very first instance due to e-filing of an appeal beyond the statutorily condonable period, particularly when such a filing has been delayed for bona fide reasons beyond the litigant’s control and when the fault was entirely at the end of the Registry of the NCLAT? We think not! ” the Supreme Court said in its September 10 ruling. items.title: Ajeet Bharti bail plea: Delhi High Court sees intense exchange between Advocate Jai Dehadrai and judge
items.summary: The hearing of YouTuber Ajeet Bharti’s anticipatory bail plea before the Delhi High Court saw some tense moments between Bharti’s counsel, Jai Anant Dehadrai and Justice Saurabh Banerjee , the judge hearing the case. It started when Dehadrai tried to hand over to the court a document containing the extracted transcript of the allegedly offending remarks made by Bharti in his YouTube video. Justice Banerjee objected to it. He said that Dehadrai could not hand over the words used by Bharti to a court of law. The judge then warned that he would issue a contempt of court notice to Dehadrai. “You cannot hand over the words used by him to a court of law. I will issue contempt notice to you. Phraseology used is not offensive according to you? Please be aware of what you are doing. It contains word which are...You can't hand over those things to the court of law. You should not, as a counsel, hand over this,” Justice Banerjee said. Justice Saurabh Banerjee, Advocate Jai Anant Dehadrai Dehadrai replied that the document merely contained a transcript of what had been alleged in the FIR and was being presented to assist the Court. He said that handing over such documents was a usual practice.
